situation (example wording): "What's the effect of politics on violent crime?", "Why is murder falling?", "safest city in the us", "clearance rates by state", "What is the homicide clearance rate in Kansas?" (a question the app declines whatever place or period is given); "us homicide trend from 1950 to 2024", "American violent crime since 2018", "SF aggravated assault per month", "What is SFPD rape clearance rate?" (the nation or San Francisco written another way)
what the app does today: The app asked which place (or which period) first and then declined; the nation written "us" or "American", and "SF", "SFPD" and "San fran", were not read as places and asked which place.
proposed behavior: A question the app declines whatever place or period is given is declined at once, with its usual sentence, and asks nothing first: a why, an effect or a cause (the explanation sentence), safest or most dangerous (P13), a state's clearance rate for a Part I crime and clearance rates by state (P18). The nation is read when written "the us", "us" before a crime word, "U.S" without its last dot or "American" before cities or a crime; San Francisco when written "SF", "SFPD" or "San fran" (the answer says: Read "SF" as "San Francisco".). The pronoun in "show us murders" and "American Indian" are not places and still ask which place. A ranking of cities in the nation with no year asks the year, as it does for a state (P05). "The annual number of" is read as "annual": a series by year (P06). A "why" is declined only in a question about crime; a "why" about the data (which states are not represented) is not an explanation request.
exact default or choices offered: No buttons for the declines; places are asked as before.
why: Scorecard 2026-11-16 (dev baseline): about 24 first questions were asked a place first when the answer was a decline, and about 22 wrote the nation or San Francisco in a form the reader missed.
status: No new decision: applies P13, P18 and the explanation rule, and changes only what the reader recognizes (coordinator 2026-11-16)
